speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us identify the cause of your blisters and ulcers, have you experienced any recent sun exposure or taken new medications lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the mucosal involvement and recent medication changes, I need to assess the extent of the skin reaction. Do you have any blisters or peeling skin on your trunk, face, or other areas besides the forearm?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: Within normal limits. Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Do you have any similar blisters or skin peeling on your face, lips, or inside your mouth?
REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct_Immunofluorescence: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Blood_Tests (Autoantibodies): Presence of desmoglein antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy and immunofluorescence results are definitive, showing the characteristic intercellular IgG deposition and acantholysis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
